divergence: Wi-Fi was never invented — the internet exists but only by cable, cafés are for coffee, and laptops are leashed to walls
story_angle: official denial that accidentally confirms everything, quoted at length
headline: FCC Chairman Confirms National Ethernet Shortage Amid 40-Minute Statement of Denial
deck: Cites 'routine maintenance' while chaos engulfs coffee shops as citizens battle for bandwidth.
article:
FCC Chairman Gerald T. Reels spent 40 minutes reciting a 14-page roster of overbooked municipal jacks from 47 cities, all while insisting no shortage existed. He pointed to July 23 commuter data and labeled the jam 'routine maintenance' on the same 12 docks already flagged in office timesheets.

Brenda Tangle, waiting to book a slot, said she had stood an hour for a single wall port. 'If this is routine, I'd hate to see what a crisis looks like.'

Footnotes in the released transcript listed cable-reel weight limits for park benches. The briefing ended with the chairman's nod; outside, café lines lengthened as users clutched cords like entry tickets.
author: Harriet Plugworth, Senior Cable Correspondent

oped.title: Ethernet Famine? Nonsense—It's Character-Building Cable Austerity
oped.author: Lord Percival Throttlewick, Honorary Cable-Length Arbiter at the Institute of Obsolete Necessities
oped.body: Chairman Reels's 40-minute denial shows the jam is ordinary upkeep, not emergency. The real problem is café idlers with floppy cords that hog ports meant for serious work. Their laptop cases snag my three-foot official cable at the Corner Percolator, leaving me standing while they fight for access. The fix is simple: outlets should accept only pre-approved short government cords sold by vetted vendors—such as my discreet side enterprise. That ends the lines and lets refined patrons sip in peace. Blame rests with sloppy cable habits, not federal intervention.

classifieds.text: FOR SALE: 12 gently tugged 100ft Cat6 cables, still warm from the 2pm rush at Bean & Byte. $150 each or trade for coffee loyalty stamps; first buyer gets the end that wasn't stepped on.

HELP WANTED: Cable referee needed at The Daily Grind. Duties include separating Ethernet tug-of-war contestants and explaining why 'routine maintenance' means no Wi-Fi ever existed. Free drip coffee, hazard pay in bandwidth minutes.
LOST & FOUND: One blue Ethernet cable last seen wrapped around a barista's ankle during yesterday's shortage scrum. Owner must describe the exact shade of desperation in their eyes to claim.

PUBLIC NOTICE: To the gentleman who unplugged my laptop mid-sentence at Central Perk, I forgive you. Please return the cable; my 40-minute FCC denial statement is due tomorrow and the wall jack is already taken.

panels.caption: FCC Chairman: 'No national Ethernet shortage after 40 minutes of this denial.'
Coffee shop brawl erupts as barista shouts, 'Last wall port! Routine maintenance took the rest.'
Man severs three cables at once: 'Maintenance done. Everyone's leashed to nothing.'

stories.headline: Ethernet Cable Futures Surge as Municipal Ports Enforce Quarterly Booking Windows
stories.deck: Firms now allocate 14 percent of IT budgets to cable reel maintenance crews
stories.article:
Procurement teams are hoarding Cat-6 spools after county ports required year-end reservations for business jacks. One firm now routes tax filings through a library 22 miles away to skip the downtown queue.

Brokerage notes now price cable drag time into forecasts; each extra 50 feet of leased line trims projected output by 3.2 percent. Facilities managers book all transfers for the overnight window at the strip-mall anchor store.
